messages.subject: [Rpy] quick advice please: Rpy or Rpy2
messages.subject_clean: [Rpy] quick advice please: Rpy or Rpy2
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am just trying to start using Rpy... but I faced the decision: Rpy or Rpy2... and I don't really get what is the difference between these 2 from the Rpy website. 
I just would like to install the one that is more suitable for me and don't fall in the situation of spend time in one and then realize the other one was better for me. If that is helpful, here is a short background about me:
I am PhD student in Ecology. I have been using R for a couple of years but mostly for its great advantages related with statistical packages. So I don't really build code in R, I mostly use the built-in commands it has. For building code I have more experience in Python and like it much more than R, it is just much more intuitive for me to code with Python. I don't consider myself an expert in Python but in general terms I would say now I have a medium level of experience with it and will increase because it is very useful for my work.

I will really appreciate any advice about practical/pragmatical differences between Rpy and Rpy2 that could help me to decide what to install.

Thanks,   
 
Jaime

The original rpy v1 is no longer being developed, so unless you need
it for some existing code using rpy (v1), go with rpy2.

> I have downloaded RPY2, but when I go to install it, I get the following
> error,
> Error Tried to guess R's HOME but no R command in the PATH

Oh, sorry, I've just noticed you're on Windows. I think rpy2 still
needs someone to step up and maintain Windows support.

If you want to try making it work, that error means that it can't find
the 'R' executable - you can temporarily edit your PATH environment
variable to include the folder where R.exe is. But there may well be
more problems beyond that, unfortunately.

Thomas

messages.subject: [Rpy] rpy2-2.2.7, rpy2-2.3.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I just pushed rpy2 2.2.7. There is only one change when compared to 
2.2.6: the egg does not report as a "dev" version any longer (issue 
#101); if this was not a problem there is no need to update.

Rpy2-2.3.0 is still work in progress, the latest effort being the memory 
management layer almost completely rewritten - some documentation for it 
is at 
http://rpy.sourceforge.net/rpy2/doc-dev/html/rinterface.html?highlight=memory#memory-management-and-garbage-collection. 
I'd encourage projects currently in development to already use 
rpy2-2.3.0 from the bitbucket repository: with the rewrite, potential 
and hard-to-track problems with in rpy2-2.2.x (and earlier) were 
identified (and presumably fixed).

Best,


Laurent

messages.subject: [Rpy] Rpy2-2.3.0beta1
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Thanks to all who downloaded the alpha1; the ratio bug reports / 
download is under 1%, and most of the bugs were fixed quickly.

One note: I moved to R-2.15.2 for tested and noted a C-API breaking 
change with that R release . It is fixed in the beta1, so try again
if you had issues with a recent development version of R and rpy2.

Best,

Laurent
